html:
The Battle of Algiers is a 1966 Italian-Algerian film by Gillo Pontecorvo about the struggle for Algeria's independence from France. It won the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival.

It shows the fight for the city of Algiers between 1954 and 1957 during the Algerian War: the bombings by the National Liberation Front (FLN), and the French paratroopers who broke its network through mass arrests and torture.

It was shot in black and white on the real streets of the Casbah, with crowds of local people and mostly non-professional actors. One of them, Saadi Yacef, had been an FLN commander in the battle and helped produce the film. The newsreel look was so convincing that the makers stated no documentary footage was used.

France banned it for years. It became a model for political cinema, and armies and rebels alike studied it; in 2003 the Pentagon screened it as the Iraq occupation began. The war's end brought the exodus of the pieds-noirs.
sum: The Battle of Algiers is a 1966 Italian-Algerian film by Gillo Pontecorvo about the struggle for Algeria's independence from France. It won the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival.
